hook.text: Germany's economy collapsed. Nazi propaganda said: 'It's the Jews.' A complex problem got a simple villain.

buildup.text: Scapegoating blames a group for complex problems, offering a simple target for public anger.

discovery.text: Scapegoats are always minorities or outsiders — groups too weak to fight back effectively.

twist.text: Scapegoating persists because it satisfies our need for simple explanations in a complex world.

climax.text: When a politician blames one group for everything, they're not solving problems — they're creating enemies.

punchline.text: Complex problems don't have simple villains.

quiz.question: Why is scapegoating an effective propaganda technique?
options: It satisfies the need for simple explanations
